title: Doubling invariant
statement: For a natural number $n$ and a Boolean list $S$, the doubling invariant holds when there is a natural number $j$ such that $S$ is the pair encoding of the list consisting of $j$ copies of `false` followed by `true`, and the list formed by prefixing `false` to the binary-bit list of $n$, with $j\leq \lceil\log_2(2n)\rceil$.
caveat: The pair encoding and the convention for the binary-bit list are not defined in the supplied material.
